title: A restore fired through the nonce path is invisible in the log
body:
The extension's ready-check restore announces itself (onRestore -> 'the container was lost between rounds; workspace restored to <sha>'), but the other live path — a tracked bash whose nonce no container knows, FactorySandboxEnv.execAttempt's ensureWorkspaceRestored -> restoreLostWorkspace — restores with no log line anywhere: the operator watching a run sees only a mysteriously slow tool round. tick cni's staging proof hit exactly this (a 139 s round whose restore was invisible). The host should hear the nonce-path restore too, or the nonce path should report which sha it rebuilt from.
evidence: harness/src/env/factory-sandbox.ts ensureWorkspaceRestored (the restore's only caller with no onRestore wiring), against harness/src/workspace/checkpoints.ts WorkspaceCheckpointOptions.onRestore
